subject.title: Bug: exec() tool strips dollar-variable patterns via undocumented template substitution

question: Should Windows exec support PowerShell `$` expansion payloads by parsing them into one-shot explicit approvals, or should OpenClaw document them as unsupported/direct-script-file-only input?
rationale: Current code intentionally rejects `$` expansion tokens in approval analysis, while the reported expectation requires a command-fidelity/security-boundary choice before automation should create another fix PR.

options.title: Use one-shot approval support
options.body: Proceed with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 or equivalent after native Windows proof, preserving the approval boundary while allowing `$` payloads through review.

options.title: Document unsupported payloads
options.body: Close the behavior as unsupported after updating exec docs to say direct PowerShell expansion strings should be put in scripts or passed through safer inputs.

options.title: Redesign Windows shell selection
options.body: Defer this issue into a broader Windows shell-contract design if maintainers want configurable shell selection or a different default invocation model.

recommendation.title: Use one-shot approval support
recommendation.body: Proceed with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/100322 or equivalent after native Windows proof, preserving the approval boundary while allowing `$` payloads through review.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent is the current-main blame owner on the inspected Windows exec analyzer/default lines in this checkout and is the most recent routing candidate for the active surface.
